title: Sharing things out equally
examples: What if some are left over?

explain.say: Look at the board. There are 12 strawberries and 3 plates. Sharing fairly means every plate gets the same. The strawberries are shared out.
Share 1 at a time. Put 1 strawberry on each plate. Every plate has 1. Keep going until all the strawberries are shared. Can you show sharing with your hands?
Keep sharing. Now each plate has 2. 6 strawberries are on the plates. 6 more are still to share. How many will each plate get?
All 12 are shared out. Each plate has 4. 12 shared between 3 is 4. This is called dividing. Every plate has the same, so it is fair. Count each plate to check.
Now share 10 grapes between 2 plates. Each plate gets 5. Today, share some buttons between 2 teddies.

faq.a: It means giving everyone exactly the same amount, so it is fair. Twelve strawberries shared by three gives four each.

faq.q: How do I share things out?
faq.a: Deal them one at a time to each group, round and round, until there are none left. Then count one group.
Dividing means sharing into equal groups. Twelve divided by three is four.

faq.q: What if there are some left over?
faq.a: Sometimes things do not share equally. The ones left over are called the remainder. Seven sweets shared by two is three each, with one left over.

faq.q: How do I check my sharing?
faq.a: Count each group. If every group has the same, you shared it equally. Add the groups back together and you get the number you started with.
asks: How do I know it is fair?

facts: Things left over after sharing equally are called the remainder.

quiz.say: Kofi shares 10 grapes between 2 friends. How many grapes does each friend get?
quiz.show: 🍇 10 grapes shared by 2 friends. How many each?
quiz.why: 5 and 5 make 10. So each friend gets 5 grapes.

quiz.say: Amira wants to share fairly. What is the best way?
quiz.show: What is the best way to share fairly?
quiz.why: Giving 1 to each person in turn keeps every group the same size.

wrong.0: The other people get none, so it is unfair.
